title: Building, mechanical, gas and electrical permits for a glass studio's furnaces, glory holes, kilns and ventilation, with inspections and the certificate of occupancy
question: I am fitting out a space with a gas-fired glass furnace, glory hole, kilns, torches and exhaust hoods. Which building and trade permits do I need in Charlottesville, what do they cost, and how do inspections and the certificate of occupancy work?
office: Neighborhood Development Services, Building Inspections Division (the City building official); City Public Permit Portal
summary: Charlottesville enforces the Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code (the 2021 code for permits filed from January 18, 2025). Installing or altering mechanical systems, fuel-gas piping, electrical wiring, plumbing or any equipment the code regulates needs a permit before work starts, and moving a glass studio into an existing building is a change of occupancy that needs a permit and a new certificate of occupancy. Apply in the City Public Permit Portal: a building permit for the fit-out, then linked Mechanical, Gas, Electrical and Plumbing permits, each from a DPOR-licensed contractor (an owner may only self-perform within the Va. Code § 54.1-1101 exemptions, which do not cover a commercial studio). Commercial (VCC) drawings go through plan review; a Type 1 commercial kitchen hood has its own permit line. Fees are $75 minimum per permit, then $75 plus project value times the base rate, plus a $10 to $50 system maintenance fee and the 2% state levy. Request inspections in the portal: sub-trade rough-ins (gas lines under pressure test, not connected), framing, finals, then the gas unlock after every gas inspection passes, with Charlottesville Gas unlocking the meter the next business day after Building Inspections notifies it. A $100 fee applies when work is not ready and to reinspections. The building official issues the certificate of occupancy within five working days of the approved final; a temporary certificate for non-residential space is $1 per square foot per month. Nothing may be used before the certificate is issued.

legal_basis.quote: Enforcement of the provisions of the Building Code for construction and rehabilitation shall be the responsibility of the local building department.

Any person aggrieved by the local building department's application of the Building Code or refusal to grant a modification to the provisions of the Building Code may appeal to the local board of Building Code appeals.
Fees may be levied by the local governing body in order to defray the cost of such enforcement and appeals.

legal_basis.quote: The applicant shall also furnish satisfactory proof that the taxes or license fees required by any county, city, or town have been paid so as to be qualified to bid upon or contract for the work for which the permit has been applied.

Application for a permit shall be made to the building official and a permit shall be obtained prior to the commencement of any of the following activities, except that applications for emergency construction, alterations, or equipment replacement shall be submitted by the end of the first working day that follows the day such work commences.

(v) water supply and distribution system, sanitary drainage system, or vent system; (vi) electric wiring; (vii) fire protection system, mechanical systems, or fuel supply systems; or (viii) any equipment regulated by the USBC.
For change of occupancy, application for a permit shall be made when a new certificate of occupancy is required by the VEBC.
Replacement of aboveground existing LP-gas containers of the same capacity in the same location and associated regulators when installed by the serving gas supplier.

The building official shall issue the certificate of occupancy within five working days after approval of the final inspection and when the building or structure or portion thereof is determined to be in compliance with this code and any pertinent laws or ordinances, or when otherwise entitled.

Upon the request of a permit holder, a temporary certificate of occupancy may be issued before the completion of the work covered by a permit, provided that such portion of a building of structure may be occupied safely prior to full completion of the building or structure without endangering life or public safety.

A certificate of occupancy may be revoked or suspended whenever the building official discovers that such certificate was issued in error or on the basis of incorrect information, or where there are repeated violations of the USBC after the certificate has been issued or when requested by the code official under Section 106.6 of the VMC.

steps.step: List the work that needs a permit
steps.who: Operator with the designer and contractors
steps.how: Under USBC § 108.1 a permit is needed before: construction or demolition; removing or adding walls; structural work; altering a required fire-rated assembly or means of egress; water, drain or vent piping; electric wiring; fire protection, mechanical or fuel supply systems; and installing any equipment the code regulates. For a hot shop that covers the furnace, glory hole and kilns and their gas piping, the oxygen and propane piping for torches, the exhaust hoods, make-up air and ventilation, the electrical service for kilns and blowers, compressed-air and water lines, and any slab or structural work. Moving the studio into an existing building is a change of occupancy that needs a permit when a new certificate of occupancy is required. Replacing an existing above-ground LP-gas container of the same size in the same place by the gas supplier is exempt. The city's residential-style exemption for replacing non-gas appliances does not apply to a commercial studio.
steps.deadline: Before work starts; emergency equipment replacement must be applied for by the end of the next working day (USBC § 108.1)
steps.quote: (v) water supply and distribution system, sanitary drainage system, or vent system; (vi) electric wiring; (vii) fire protection system, mechanical systems, or fuel supply systems; or (viii) any equipment regulated by the USBC.

steps.step: Settle zoning and any Development Review first
steps.who: Operator; NDS Zoning and Development Review
steps.how: Confirm the use is permitted in the district and whether site changes trigger Development Review (see glass_studio_zoning_use). The city says an approved Final Site Plan must exist before construction-related permits such as building permits when Development Review applies, while a change of use with no site-access change goes directly to building-permit review. In an Architectural Design Control, Historic Conservation or Entrance Corridor district, exterior work (including new exhaust stacks or louvers visible from the street) may need a Certificate of Appropriateness first; where a building permit is required, work under a Certificate is lawful only with the building permit.
steps.quote: An approved Final Site Plan—Major or Minor—is required before applying for constructionrelated permits such as bonds, VESMP permits, Land Disturbance permits, Affordable Housing Certification, or Building Permits.

steps.step: Hire DPOR-licensed contractors; an owner cannot self-permit a commercial studio
steps.who: Operator; licensed building, mechanical, gas, electrical and plumbing contractors
steps.how: Before a permit is issued the applicant must give a Virginia DPOR contractor license number or file a written statement that the work is exempt. The owner exemptions in Va. Code § 54.1-1101(A) cover an owner's own primary residence and certain rental dwellings, not a commercial fit-out, so each trade permit will carry a licensed contractor. The application also asks for proof that city taxes and license fees are paid, and contractors need a City business license (Commissioner of the Revenue). Each trade or contractor files a separate application.
steps.quote: Fill out separate applications for each trade or contractor.

steps.who: Architect or engineer (DPOR-licensed) and the equipment suppliers
steps.how: The Building Permit Application asks whether the Virginia Residential Code or the Virginia Construction Code applies (a studio is VCC), the estimated cost, square footage per floor, height, stories, whether the building is sprinklered, and the architect or engineer's DPOR number. Plan on drawings that show the occupancy classification (the furnace room, classroom, retail and any cafe may be different groups), egress, the furnace, glory hole and kiln installations with their manufacturers' listings and clearances, fuel-gas piping sized for the connected load, oxygen and propane piping and storage, exhaust hoods, make-up air and ventilation, electrical loads, plumbing and any grease interceptor for a cafe. The Mandatory Inspections sheet notes that Chapter 17 of the VCC requires special inspectors under a registered design professional for the types of work in Section 1705. The city posts the Building Inspections' Climatic and Geographic Design Criteria and an ICC Plan Review Services flyer; what role ICC plays in the city's commercial plan review is not stated. Upload files of 5 MB or less with the application and larger ones afterwards.
steps.quote: Tax Map and Parcel _______________________ Bldg Code: VRC or VCC (circle)

steps.step: Apply for the building permit in the City Public Permit Portal
steps.who: Applicant (owner, lessee or contractor) with a portal account
steps.how: Create an account at permits.charlottesville.gov/portal, click Create New Application, choose the application type and subtype, add the address, contacts and contractor, describe the project and its estimated cost, upload files, agree to the terms and submit; note the permit number. The paper Building Permit Application (which also covers Tank Removal, Demolition, Fire Sprinkler/Line and Tent permits) is still posted, but the city's Inspection Results Cheat Sheet says the city has switched to a fully digital permit submission and inspection system. The NDS page warns that the city does not email invoices for permit fees except on request; pay only in the portal. Building Inspections moved to the first floor of City Hall (605 E Main Street) on January 26, 2026; online service is preferred and appointments are encouraged.
steps.deadline: An application not pursued in good faith is abandoned six months after filing (USBC § 108.8)
steps.fee: Building permit: $75 minimum, then $75 plus project value times the base rate (BR) above $1,500 of project value
steps.quote: 13. Make note of the permit number in the Application Created screen. The permit will now be on your dashboard for further tracking.

steps.step: Add linked Mechanical, Gas, Electrical and Plumbing permits (and a Fire Sprinkler/Line or Tank permit if needed)
steps.how: In the portal choose Create New Application, then Linked Application, search for the building permit and add the trade application with the contractor's details. The fee schedule lists separate Electrical, Mechanical, Plumbing and Gas permit fees ($75 minimum each, then by project value), a Fire Protection permit, a Tank (UST or AGST) removal or installation permit, and a 'Commercial Kitchen Hood - Type 1 only' permit ($75 minimum) for a cafe with grease-producing cooking. Equipment hoods over furnaces and glory holes are mechanical work under the mechanical permit; confirm with Building Inspections how it classes a non-grease hot-shop hood. Where the building has or needs sprinklers, the fire line to the building uses the Fire Protection permit fee plus the Utilities Department tap fee.
steps.fee: Electrical, Mechanical, Plumbing, Gas, Fire Protection and Commercial Kitchen Hood (Type 1) permits: $75 minimum each; over $1,500 of project value, $75 plus project value multiplied by BR
steps.quote: 3. Click the “Linked Application” option under Application Type

steps.step: Plan review, corrections and fee payment
steps.who: NDS Building Inspections plan reviewers; applicant
steps.how: The building official examines the documents within a reasonable time and either approves or gives written reasons for denial; revised files are uploaded through Open Plan Review in the portal (email permits@charlottesville.gov if the upload option is closed). Pay in the portal under My Fees. Every permit carries a Permit System Maintenance Fee ($10 under $200, $20 for $200 to $499.99, $35 for $500 to $1,000, $50 over $1,000) and the 2% state levy. The base rate (BR) prints illegibly in the scanned schedule; use the city's Permit Fees Calculator page or ask Building Inspections. A permit is not issued until the fees are paid. An amendment after issuance costs $75 minimum plus the rate on added value.
steps.deadline: Within a reasonable time after filing (USBC §§ 109.4, 110.1); no local turnaround is published
steps.fee: Permit System Maintenance Fee $10 to $50; 2.00% state levy; amendment $75 minimum
steps.quote: NOTE: The permit must be set to accept new files. If you see a message indicating the upload option is not available, contact permits@charlottesville.gov to assist with re-opening the permit.

steps.step: Post the permit, keep the stamped plans on site and start within six months
steps.how: Download the approved plans from Open Plan Review (Approved Plan Documents) and keep a hard copy of the city's RED stamped plans on site for every inspection. Post the permit card where it is visible from the road. Work must start within six months of issuance and not stop for six months, or the building official may revoke the permit; extensions of up to a year each can be requested in writing. Working without a permit is charged at twice the permit fee in the fee schedule, and a stop-work order carries its own fee.
steps.deadline: Start within six months of issuance (USBC § 110.6)
steps.fee: Working without a permit: permit fee x 2 (NDS Fee Schedule)
steps.quote: The City of Charlottesville approved RED stamped plans must be on site for all inspections (Hard Copy).

steps.step: Request and pass the inspections in order, including the gas pressure test
steps.who: Permit holder and trade contractors; NDS Building Inspections (434-970-3008, Inspections@charlottesville.gov)
steps.how: Request each inspection in the portal (My Inspections, calendar icon) before covering work. The city's minimum list in typical order: footing, projection, foundation, slab, sub-trade rough-ins (mechanical, electrical, plumbing and gas, with all gas lines run to each appliance but not connected, under pressure with the correct gauge and each line sized for the appliance BTUs), framing, insulation, water and sewer lines, trenches, then the finals. Exterior natural gas trenches to the meter are inspected by Charlottesville Gas and power service from the pole to the meter by Dominion Energy; all other electrical, gas and water trenches are inspected by Building Inspections. The gas unlock inspection comes after all gas inspections pass and all appliances are installed and approved; Building Inspections then notifies Charlottesville Gas, which unlocks the meter by the end of the next business day. Provide ladders, scaffolds and test equipment. Results appear under Tasks on the permit record.
steps.deadline: Before work is concealed (USBC § 113.1.2); the city must inspect within two working days of a request or accept third-party reports (USBC § 113.7)
steps.fee: Not Ready fee $100; reinspection fee $100 (starts after the second inspection of the same violation)
steps.quote: Gas - all lines run and installed to each appliance location, but not connected to the appliance, must be under pressure using correct gauge, proper nail plates installed, each line sized correctly for the appliance BTU's.

steps.step: Use pre-approved third-party inspectors if you want (voluntary)
steps.who: Owner or permit holder; an inspector on the city's pre-approved list
steps.how: The city's written policy lets owners and licensed contractors have gas, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, framing and other listed inspections done by private inspectors the building official has pre-approved (the current list is posted as '3rd Party Approved Inspectors 6-4-2026'). Reports go on the city's form with photos within the policy's time limit, and the permit holder must check that every inspection is posted to the permit. The program does not cover Chapter 17 special inspections, fire detection, protection or suppression systems, other departments' inspections or elevators, and a third-party inspector cannot clear a violation the city has cited.
steps.deadline: Report within 24 hours of the inspection (city policy)
steps.fee: Paid to the inspector; the policy allows the building official to set a flat city fee per third-party inspection if needed (none in the fee schedule)
steps.quote: All 3rd party inspectors must be pre-approved by the building official prior to performing 3rd party inspection.

steps.step: Pass the final inspections and get the certificate of occupancy
steps.how: The building final follows approved finals on every trade permit (mechanical, electrical, plumbing, gas, sprinkler), all fees paid, utilities connected and working. The building official issues the certificate of occupancy within five working days after the approved final. No part of the studio may be used for any purpose before it is issued; the Blue Ridge Health District also requires the occupancy permit before its pre-opening inspection of a cafe, and the Fire Marshal's Office inspects assembly and restaurant occupancies after they open. A temporary certificate may be issued on request when part of the building is safe to occupy: for non-residential uses the fee is $1 per square foot per month or partial month. A certificate can be suspended or revoked for repeated code violations.
steps.deadline: Certificate of occupancy within five working days after approval of the final inspection (USBC § 116.1)
steps.fee: Temporary Certificate of Occupancy, non-residential: $1/sq ft per month; the fee schedule also lists a fee to 'Issue Certificate of Occupancy not required by USBC' for a new tenant who needs a CO for VDH or insurance (amount not legible)
steps.quote: Prior to occupancy or change of occupancy of a building or structure, a certificate of occupancy shall be obtained in accordance with this section.

steps.step: Appeal a denial, a code interpretation or a stop-work order
steps.who: Applicant; Local Board of Building Code Appeals; State Building Code Technical Review Board
steps.how: A written appeal goes to the local board within 30 calendar days of the decision (Building Code Board of Appeals application, fee in the NDS schedule), then to the State Review Board within 21 calendar days of the local board's decision. A denial must come with written reasons.
steps.deadline: 30 calendar days to the local board (USBC § 119.5); 21 calendar days to the State Review Board (USBC § 119.8)
steps.fee: Building Code Board of Appeals application fee: per the NDS Fee Schedule (amount not legible in the scanned PDF)
steps.quote: Any person aggrieved by the local building department's application of the Building Code or refusal to grant a modification to the provisions of the Building Code may appeal to the local board of Building Code appeals.

caveats: The city publishes no guidance specific to glass furnaces, glory holes or kilns. Which permit (mechanical vs. a separate equipment line) covers a custom gas-fired furnace, whether the city will ask for listed equipment or an engineer's evaluation of unlisted, shop-built furnaces, and how it classifies a non-grease hood over a glory hole are questions for Building Inspections.

The fee schedule is a scanned PDF. The base rate (BR) that permit fees multiply is not legible; the city's Permit Fee Calculations page is a calculator whose content did not come through as text. Rows for 'Stop Work Order Fee', 'Issue Certificate of Occupancy not required by USBC' and the Board of Appeals application fee cannot be matched to amounts with confidence.

The Mandatory Inspections sheet is written for one- and two-family dwellings and gives 434-970-3182 to schedule inspections; the Building Inspections page gives 434-970-3008 and the portal. Commercial projects may need more inspections than the sheet lists, including Chapter 17 special inspections.

The ICC Plan Review Services flyer is posted on the Building Inspections page without explanation; whether the city sends commercial plans to ICC, or expects applicants to buy a third-party review, is not stated.
USBC quotes for §§ 108.8, 109.4, 110.1, 110.6, 113.1.2, 113.7 and 119 are cited from the sections as read for building_permit_residential.json; only §§ 108 and 116 were re-read for this file.

The Blue Ridge Health District's pre-opening inspection for a cafe requires the occupancy permit first, and the Fire Marshal's Office inspects restaurants and assembly spaces: sequence the certificate of occupancy before the health and fire steps.
Dominion Energy's electrical service connection and Charlottesville Gas's service line are separate from the building permits (see glass_studio_utilities_and_environment).
